newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips hits new highs as Q2 earnings please.
newsitem.headline: Philips hits new highs as Q2 earnings please.

text.p: Shares in Philips Electronics ,Europe's biggest consumer electronics group, hit new highs on Thursday as the company reported second-quarter earnings far above market expectations.
Philips said net profit from ordinary operations more than doubled to 693 million guilders ($337 million) from 304 million in the same period of 1996.
The group said all product sectors contributed to the rise despite further price erosion of six percent over the first half of this year in the fiercely competitive electronics industry.
Chief Financial Officer Jan Hommen said the improvement reflected continuing efforts to cut costs, eliminate losses and obtain a better return from the group's assets.
"The benefits of the restructuring programmes are beginning to show in our operating performance. More is still to be done and more is still to come," he said.
Philips' earnings roundly outstripped analysts' forecasts for the quarter of 429 to 540 million guilders, catapulting the company's shares to new highs.
The shares initially rose over eight percent to a high of 177.00 guilders and by 1235 GMT they were up 5.90 guilders or 3.64 percent at 168.00.
Analysts said the strong second-quarter performance would force them to take a fresh look at their full-year estimates.
"The results are much better than expected and what is surprising is the enormous improvement in Europe. We will raise our earnings estimates," said Steven Vrolijk of ING Barings.

Philips said it remained committed to achieving its previously stated goal of double digit growth in operating income, a positive cash flow of over one billion guilders in 1997, and a 24 percent return on net assets in the longer term.
Hommen said Philips had fallen short of the latter target in the first half of 1997 with a return on net assets of 15.6 pct.
But he noted that the group's operating margin -- operating profit as a percentage of sales -- had risen to 6.7 percent in the second quarter of 1997 from 5.2 percent in the first.
The core consumer products division was an isolated area of weakness in the second quarter, with operating profits dipping to 62 million guilders from 206 million in the first.

Hommen said this was largely due to a U.S. advertising campaign to promote the Philips name -- part of a wider global brand-building drive -- and up-front costs for the launch of a new lightweight GSM mobile phone, Genie, later this year.
Philips still expects its consumer telephones business -- recently grouped in a joint venture with Lucent Technologies to become profitable in the fourth quarter of 1997.
"Once we begin to ship the Genie it will have a dramatic impact on our earnings," Hommen said.
Philips said the outlook looked bright for its semiconductor business, with strong demand and an apparent end to price erosion in the industry by the end of the second quarter.
Hommen said the group's factories were running at high capacity and that Philips would squeeze more capacity from existing plants.
The professional products division moved back into the black in the second quarter of 1997 with an operating profit of 149 million guilders after a first-quarter loss of 54 million.
Hommen said this was largely a result of strong growth in the volume of sales of monitors for personal computers, even though prices had remained under pressure.
Philips is currently conducting a strategic business review but does not plan to go public with the results before early next year.
Hommen said Philips' business units and product divisions had recently submitted five-year strategic plans which senior management was now studying.
"I would think that some time early next year or maybe a little bit later we will be in a position to really decide strategically what it is that we want to do," he said.

New chairman Cor Boonstra has stressed that enhancing profitability was his first priority and that the strategic reshaping of Philips' business portfolio -- which runs from toasters to X-ray machines -- will follow later. ($ = 2.054 Dutch Guilders)
